terms.gloss: tiredness from the difference in the hours
terms.comment: A description of ours: no reference work has a word for jet lag (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini, Andresian searched). It is made of classical words: lassitūdō, weariness (Plaut., Cic.), and discrīmen, the difference between two things. In speech the plain sentence is better: nōndum hōrīs hujus regiōnis assuēvimus; see the examples.

phrases.english: We’re not used to the hours here yet.

phrases.latin: Ex hōrārum discrīmine adhūc lassī sumus; domī enim jam media nox est.
phrases.english: We’re still tired from the time difference: at home it’s already midnight.

phrases.latin: Puer noctū vigilat, interdiū dormit: nōndum hōrīs nostrīs assuēvit.
phrases.english: The boy is awake at night and sleeps by day: he isn’t used to our hours yet.

sources: Lewis & Short: lassitudo · Lewis & Short: discrimen · Lewis & Short: assuesco
